sources.quote: the claim is a flat line at $1/8$

There is no zero of the Riemann zeta function, of any Dirichlet L-function (any modulus, any character, uniformly) or of any finite-order Hecke L-function over Q(sqrt(-3)) in the half-plane Re(s) > 7/8
Not a proof of RH (1/2). The 7/8 boundary is not included.
If correct this is among the largest results in analytic number theory in a century, so the bar is extraordinary.
